judgment.notes: Apply N001's distance-preserving-map clause with domain I⊆Eucl(1), target Eucl(n+1), and g(t)=(x0,t), using the standard identification of real numbers with one-tuples. The displayed distance calculation verifies its premise. Apply monotonicity in Eucl(n+1) to g(I)⊆F. N006 concerns exactly the interval I used here. There are no external E/M applications.

For t,u∈I the first n coordinate differences vanish and the remaining distance is |t-u|. The chosen x0∈E gives g(I)⊆E×I=F. Hence N001 and N006 imply dimH(F)≥dimH(g(I))=1. Under D=0, D is finite and D+1=1, giving every clause of N007. The calculation also holds for the empty coordinate sum when n=0. No limiting operation or regularity assumption occurs.
